newsitem.title: UK: U.Utilities board to meet Tuesday - report.
newsitem.headline: U.Utilities board to meet Tuesday - report.

text.p: Britain's United Utilities Plc will hold a board meeting on Tuesday in response to calls from some investors for its chairman Sir Desmond Pitcher to step down, the Financial Times said on Monday.
The newspaper said Pitcher's fate was in the balance ahead of the meeting, which it said advisers had described as unscheduled rather than emergency.
No-one at United Utilities was immediately available for comment.
Pitcher's surprise sacking of chief executive Brian Staples last month fueled concerns about a board split and prompted some investors to demand that he step down.

The Financial Times said that there had been meetings over the weekend during which Pitcher had been fighting to persuade boardroom colleagues to support him on Tuesday and present a united front to shareholders.
Pitcher, once considered the highest-paid of all the heads of the privatised utilities, has a reputation for hands-on management and an autocractic style.
On Friday, a company spokeswoman declined to comment on reports that investors were calling for Pitcher to take a non-executive post by the end of this year.
The Financial Times said the dispute intensified when it emerged that Sir Peter Middleton, a non-executive director, had been canvassing opinion in London financial circles on Pitcher's position.
United Utilities was formed when water and sewerage company North West Water took over electricity company Norweb in 1995.

The company disappointed the market in May with annual profits below expectations while it took an 83 million pounds ($131.8 million) charge for losses on operations in Bangkok, which Staples then described as "a serious disappointment".
It warned in July when Staples left that current trade was slightly below analysts' expectations. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717 ($ = 0.629 British Pounds)
